turns.assessment: The simultaneous loss of many unrelated services, including svc261, localizes to the sole common working-path element, roadm.S01. Concurrent AMP_INPUT_LOS on two different outgoing OMS directions from S01 indicates that channels were blocked before those amplifiers; this is inconsistent with a client, line-interface, or OTN-switch fault and is best explained by failure of a shared ROADM WSS input port.

proposals.rationale: A failed WSS input port at roadm.S01 can block all channels arriving on the common degree and therefore remove light on multiple outgoing degrees. This explains the broad correlated service outage and the simultaneous AMP_INPUT_LOS alarms on S01->S04 and S01->S15.

clarify.assessment: The two outgoing-degree losses show that one common S01 WSS input port can be responsible, but they do not identify which incoming degree failed. Inputs from S04 and S15 are less plausible because they would require same-degree turnaround for one observed output, while S12, S13, and S20 remain indistinguishable from the supplied evidence. A specific repair location is therefore not justified.

llm_alone.decision: commit not to one place (5 locations); reported as a set

score.why: truth not in the reported set
